neighbours.label: The modal-perfect 'have' (or 'instead') that states an alternative outcome which did not happen, vs the same events told as plain fact
fire: Experts say that if the dam had not failed, the valley could have avoided the worst flooding.
Looking back, the company could have survived the recession with a smaller loan.
Prices would have been far lower if the tariff had never been introduced.
Many fans believe the striker could have won the title with a different coach.
If the vaccine had arrived a year earlier, thousands of lives could have been saved.
Historians argue that the empire could have lasted another century without the civil war.
Had the bank not lent them money, the farm would have been sold at auction.
Without the rescue crew, the hikers could have frozen on the ridge overnight.
quiet: Experts say the dam failed in March and the valley suffered the worst flooding.
Looking back, the company survived the recession with a small loan.
Prices rose sharply after the tariff was introduced last spring.
Many fans believe the striker won the title thanks to the new coach.
The vaccine arrived in the spring, and thousands of people lined up for it.
Historians note that the empire lasted another century after the civil war.
The bank lent them money, and the farm stayed in the family.
The rescue crew reached the hikers on the ridge just after midnight.

predictions: 'could/would/might have' after an unreal condition 0.3-0.7; the same events stated as what actually happened under 0.1.
notes: Card: ' have' in 'higher than it would have been if', 'did not exist', 'could have kept', ' instead', 'went its own way'. Probe: 'if the bridge had not been built, the town could have stayed' 0.662 (peak ' have'), 'separate ways' 0.392, 'instead started' 0.273, 'would have closed' 0.195; factual retellings 0.011-0.116.
